claims: The 2/1 roster maximises earning potential (about 243 days a year), but the highest-paying rosters are those with longer swings (3/1 or 4/1).
whys: The answer contradicts itself. A 3/1 or 4/1 roster works a larger share of the year than 2/1, so 2/1 cannot be the roster that maximises earnings. The 243 days figure is also hard-coded rather than derived.

claims: Under the Mining Industry Award, overtime is generally paid at time-and-a-half for the first 2 hours and double time after that. Many mining enterprise agreements offer annualised salaries that include overtime.
whys: The overtime multipliers and the 2-hour trigger are hard-coded and do not cite the Mining Industry Award 2020 clause. They need checking against the current award. 'Many mining enterprise agreements' is a population claim with no source.
constants: an award-overtime constant for the Mining Industry Award (MA000011) with its clause reference

whys: The FY is hard-coded and stale. The $150,000 example in the same section uses calculatePayBreakdown, which is the FY2026-27 engine, and it is labelled FY{SITE_CONFIG.financialYear} (2026-27). I could not change it because the rules forbid editing years.

claims: LAFHA of "$50 to $100 per day on-site, adding $7,000 to $14,000 per year in tax-free income on a 2/1 roster"
whys: The figures don't add up. The page says a 2/1 roster is about 243 days a year. At $50 to $100 a day, that comes to about $12,150 to $24,300, not $7,000 to $14,000. The claim that LAFHA is tax-free also clashes with the FAQ, which says LAFHA is a fringe benefit taxed to the employer under FBT and that only the exempt food and accommodation parts reduce the taxable value.
constants: lib/constants/fifo-pay.ts (next to LAFHA_STATUTORY_FOOD); the roster day counts should be derived, not typed

claims: "Most FIFO employers cover the cost of flights"; the travel allowance "is generally taxable unless the employer books and pays for travel directly, in which case it is a fringe benefit to the employer"
whys: "Most FIFO employers" is a population claim with no source. Also, travel the employer books and pays for directly is not an allowance, and FIFO flights are often exempt from FBT under the otherwise-deductible rule. The sentence mixes up two different things.
The range is hard-coded and has no source or date.
constants: ATO travel allowance vs LAFHA guidance (cited in lib/constants/fifo-pay.ts comments)

claims: Overtime on 12-hour shifts "can add $20,000–$40,000 per year above the base salary"
whys: This is the site's own estimate. It has no source and no worked basis (no hourly rate or number of overtime hours).
constants: derive from an example in lib/constants/fifo-pay.ts

claims: "Adding tax-free LAFHA of $10,000 per year brings the effective take-home to approximately ..."
whys: The $10,000 is a hard-coded literal. The example also inherits the 'LAFHA is tax-free' claim, which clashes with the FAQ: LAFHA is a fringe benefit taxed to the employer under FBT, and only the exempt food and accommodation parts reduce its taxable value.

The 12% is typed into the text, but the amounts next to it are computed from SUPER_GUARANTEE.rate. If the constant changes, the text and the computed figures will disagree. It should render from SUPER_GUARANTEE.rate.
